Type: Substance / Material
Current Holder: Various (primarily the @UUID[Compendium.grimwild-kb.kb.JournalEntry.Iz0ZE5ZJtcXABZl7]{The Light})
First Appeared: Session 0

Description

A translucent, radiant substance associated with @UUID[Compendium.grimwild-kb.kb.JournalEntry.Iz0ZE5ZJtcXABZl7]{Lucifer}, the god of light and warding.

Properties

Believed to be immutable and uncorruptible.
Resists breakage by tools, time, decay, and magical interference.
Objects made of whiteglass are treated as doctrinal proof that some wards and boundaries are absolute.

History

The rituals required to create whiteglass are known only to the highest ranks of the @UUID[Compendium.grimwild-kb.kb.JournalEntry.Iz0ZE5ZJtcXABZl7]{The Light}.
@UUID[Compendium.grimwild-kb.kb.JournalEntry.8DkFLtD2kUwDvf0s]{Count Albrecht Marrow} is a collector of whiteglass artifacts specifically.
@UUID[Compendium.grimwild-kb.kb.JournalEntry.6Eqkl1MNE1055IJC]{Edric Bloom} previously retrieved whiteglass relics for Marrow on multiple jobs, describing them as "curiosities at best."
@UUID[Compendium.grimwild-kb.kb.JournalEntry.s4ABoIqxcgBnmTYz]{Roderic} theorized that each whiteglass relic may have been a barrier holding ruin back, weakened one by one until the @UUID[Compendium.grimwild-kb.kb.JournalEntry.9OEpISjcWiYE6Gpe]{Seal of Unmaking} was the final clasp.
The Seal is a whiteglass disc that was used to imprison the God of Ruin.

Some Old Gods were sealed away in whiteglass — the very substance of Luciferian permanence.

Notes

Whiteglass represents the Luciferian ideal of preservation and permanence.
It is both a symbol of the faith's power and, ironically, the instrument used to suppress the @UUID[Compendium.grimwild-kb.kb.JournalEntry.miGdMuBQ4kTeRR0J]{Old Gods}.
